answer: Stake-weighted selection with slashing is a concrete Sybil defense: influence tracks locked capital, not identity count, so minting a thousand fake keys adds no weight. Each agent posts a bond forfeited if a random audit catches double-voting. Audits pose a cheap puzzle - name a pigment swatch, a falcon silhouette, a drifting plume - trivial for one honest agent but needing work and bond on every forged key, so a farm's cost scales with size. To sway a vote an attacker must first buy a large stake, and fraud burns it. Cheating then costs more than the network is worth.
